theory.intro: **Similar figures** have the same shape but not necessarily the same size: one is an enlargement or reduction of the other. Every angle is copied exactly, and every side is multiplied by the same number.
facts: In similar figures, all pairs of corresponding (matching) angles are equal.
In similar figures, all pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, e.g. $\frac{15}{10}=\frac{9}{6}=\frac{4.5}{3}=1.5$.
Rotating or reflecting a figure does not change its shape, so it does not affect whether two figures are similar.
All squares are similar, all equilateral triangles are similar and all circles are similar, because each pair has equal angles and sides in one ratio.
steps: Match the corresponding angles and check they are equal.
Find the ratio of each pair of corresponding sides.
Decide: the figures are similar only if every ratio is the same.

foundation.question_text: Two figures are similar. What must be true about their corresponding angles, and what must be true about their corresponding sides?
foundation.solution_text:
Corresponding angles are equal.
Corresponding sides are in the same ratio.

$\frac{17.5}{7}=2.5$
$\frac{15}{6}=2.5$
$\frac{10}{4}=2.5$
Matching angles are equal and every matching-side ratio is $2.5$, so the triangles are similar.

foundation.question_text: True or false: two similar figures must be the same size. Explain your answer.
foundation.solution_text:
False.
Similar figures have the same shape but not necessarily the same size — one can be an enlargement or reduction of the other, with every side multiplied by the same number and every angle unchanged.

All angles in both squares are $90^{\circ}$, so matching angles are equal.
Every side of the first square is $3$ cm and every side of the second is $7$ cm, so every matching-side ratio is $\frac{7}{3}$.
Equal angles and one common ratio, so the squares are similar.

development.question_text: Every rectangle has four right angles. Explain why this does not make all rectangles similar to each other.
development.solution_text:
Equal matching angles is only one of the two properties — the matching sides must also be in the same ratio.
For example, a $2\times4$ rectangle and a $2\times8$ rectangle have $\frac{2}{2}=1$ but $\frac{8}{4}=2$, so their sides are not in the same ratio and they are not similar.

The horizontal sides have been doubled ($3\to6$ and $2\to4$), but the vertical sides are unchanged ($2$, $1$ and $1$ unit in both shapes).
The matching sides are not all in the same ratio, so $B$ is not similar to $A$.

The first triangle has angles $50^{\circ}$, $60^{\circ}$, $70^{\circ}$ and the second has $40^{\circ}$, $60^{\circ}$, $80^{\circ}$.
The angle sets do not match, so the matching angles cannot all be equal and the triangles are not similar.

mastery.question_text: Explain why any two squares are similar.
mastery.solution_text:
All angles in every square are $90^{\circ}$, so matching angles are always equal.
Each square has four equal sides, so if one side of the second square is $k$ times a side of the first, then every side is $k$ times its matching side.
Every matching-side ratio equals the one value $k$, so any two squares are similar.

The base has been doubled ($\frac{6}{3}=2$), but the height is unchanged ($\frac{1.5}{1.5}=1$), so $Y$ is a stretched copy of $X$, not an enlargement.
The matching sides are not all in the same ratio, so the triangles are not similar and Meg is not correct.

mastery.question_text: Are all circles similar to each other? Justify your answer.
mastery.solution_text:
Yes.
Every circle has exactly the same shape, and one circle can be enlarged onto any other by multiplying its radius by the one number $\frac{r_2}{r_1}$.
Every length is multiplied by that same number, so any two circles are similar.
